Scratch Lean files go in a fresh temp dir of your own (`mktemp -d`), checked with `cd /Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern/formal && ~/.elan/bin/lake env lean /path/to/scratch.lean` (start with `import Ern.MM23.Horrors` and `open Ern Ern.MM03 Ern.MM23 Ern.MM23.Horrors`; modules are built).

Source: `/Users/guygouri/Downloads/ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md` §3 (cases H01–H17, expected verdicts) and §0 rule 8 (H15, H16 encoded with the obtained verdict and marked "écart connu", never presented as passed; H14 and H17 not encoded, classified). Check: (1) each case statement says what the material's "Attendu" says for that case — not weaker (e.g. a property proved on a state where it holds trivially, a conclusion that restates a hypothesis), not about a different step; (2) each case is really an execution translated by `simulation` (is `sim_of`/`simulation` actually applied to the run that contains the step under test, or only to some other run?); (3) the soundness of the runner (`step3exec_sound`, `srun_sound`, `simRun_of`, `sim_of`) — any gap would make every case unsound; (4) the auto-layout respects the obligations it must (`NewLayout` is checked per step by decide inside `Oblig` — confirm), and does not make a case vacuous (e.g. H03 pinned leaf, H16 offsets); (5) H15/H16 marked "écart connu" in docstrings and not presented as passed; (6) whether H02's "aucun programme sûr n'y parvient" is covered by more than the inactivity of one block (see `reset_kills_blocks`).

Every finding needs evidence: a quote, a decided Lean statement, or command output. No evidence, no finding. Do not ask for additions beyond the task. Return: verdict (block / changes / ok), then each finding with severity, location (file:line), cause (formalization error, missing coverage or spec defect) and evidence. Be concise; under 900 words.

@AGENTS.md

## Claude Code

You implement. The Review section applies to you only when asked.
Before coding, list the spec passages the task covers and read them in full.

# AGENTS.md

Claude Code implements. Codex reviews. Both follow this file.

## Source of truth

- `specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics. Before acting, read the spec text the task depends on. Never rely on memory, summaries, comments or earlier sessions.
- Never restate spec content in code comments or agent files. Point to its location.
- Spec beats code. If the spec is ambiguous, contradictory or silent on something the task needs: stop and report the exact passage with a concrete example of the problem. Never pick an interpretation yourself.
- Representation choices (structure or inductive type, function or relation) are yours when they change no accepted program and no behavior. A choice that does is a semantic question: stop and report.

## Scope

- Do exactly the task. No unrequested features, generalization, refactoring or "robustness" additions. Put suggestions in the report.
- Do not edit `specs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `formal/DESIGN.md` unless the task says so.

## Lean

- The Lake project is in `formal/`. `formal/DESIGN.md` governs how to formalize, never what the semantics is. Propose design decisions it does not settle in your report; never take them silently.
- Every definition or theorem that encodes a spec rule cites the rule's location in its docstring.
- A definition says what its rule says. Never make a definition more permissive, add an unjustified hypothesis or narrow a theorem's domain to obtain a proof.
- Never change a theorem statement, or a definition it depends on, to make a proof go through. If stuck, stop and report the goal state.
- Never use `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`.
- Every `.lean` file under `formal/` is part of the build target.
- Done means:
  - `lake build` (in `formal/`) succeeds;
  - this prints nothing: `grep -rnE '\b(sorry|admit|native_decide)\b|^\s*axiom\b' --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake .`
  - for each theorem completed by the task, `#print axioms` lists nothing beyond `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

## Report

Spec passages implemented (by location), what changed, what is unproven or open, spec problems found.

## Review (Codex)

Adversarial and read-only. For each change, check:

- It says exactly what the spec says: not stronger, not weaker. Read definitions, hypotheses and quantifiers, not only proofs. A theorem that holds because a definition is too permissive or its hypotheses are unsatisfiable is blocking.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.
